## PROVEN campaign structure, that works!

Section: How to navigate ads post-Andromeda  
Source: https://www.skool.com/theadsclinic/classroom/8995064f?md=5c69d6d7bd1c4ba886bf28473cd45188

*Video: video link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rKLhdBK6St8&t=1195s (no transcript available).*

#### Lesson text

The Meta Andromeda Update has left many advertisers (especially small and medium-sized businesses) feeling confused about what’s changed, how to adapt, and whether their current strategies still work. 

In this full guide, Nick Boddington and Olivia Tutt break down exactly what Andromeda means for your ad accounts, budgets, and creative testing. 

We cover:   
✅ What Meta Andromeda actually is (in plain English)   
✅ How AI and Advantage+ campaigns are changing ad performance  
✅ The best account structure for small and medium-sized businesses   
✅ How to test creatives and concepts efficiently, even on small budgets   
✅ Why you don’t need to panic or rebuild everything overnight   
✅ Practical examples of how to scale from £20/day budgets

Got question, click the post below and ask away...

## What to do if Meta spends on ONE AD only

Source: https://www.skool.com/theadsclinic/classroom/8995064f?md=ee6f371fde1f49d19feb8e4d7a592545

#### Lesson text

The most frustrating experiences in Meta advertising: when the platform spends all your budget on a single ad and ignores the rest. 

Nick explains how Meta’s delivery algorithm actually works, why ads don’t receive equal spending, and, most importantly, what you should about it.

## How to set up Budget Scheduling

Section: Utilising Your Budget  
Source: https://www.skool.com/theadsclinic/classroom/8995064f?md=aef952b77166408b834a1860cfb1278d

*Video: lesson video hosted in Skool.*

#### Lesson text

Budget Scheduling can be ideal for scaling spend during high-traffic periods, sales events, or times when your audience is most active, without needing to manually adjust budgets.

Use it when you’ve got data showing clear performance patterns (like stronger weekend sales or weekday conversions). Avoid it for new campaigns as sudden budget shifts can reset performance.

Think of it as giving your ads a smart rhythm, spending more when results are likely to be best, and conserving budget when they’re not.

Give it a go and let us know how you get on!

### Video transcript (cleaned)

[0:00] Hello everyone. I thought I would jump on and tell you a little bit about budget scheduling and how you can do this. There's a couple of things to bear in mind. We really do not recommend you turning ads on and off so it over a weekend period because it really messes with the optimisation. So the ads will be working, they'll optimise a few days and then get up to there, you know, the peak performance and then you'll turn them back off again of the weekend and then as Monday rolls back around again, you'll have the same problem about results being slower over the first half of the week. So there is a way you can come back this, you can do something called budget scheduling as I just mentioned where it increases ad spend over a certain period of time and it is a very manual labour job to do it but if it's something that's going to work for your business then you might as well try it and give it a go. Now we've been interested in this a couple of times, we've not seen enough shift in performance that we're going to do it across all of our accounts but we do have it on for a couple and we're, you know, seeing the performance jump slightly so you might as well give it a go. So what you need to do is come into your campaign and go to ad set level and when you're in here under the budget and scheduling section at the bottom you will see a show more settings. Click in here and you will find the budget scheduling editor. So in here you need to select on for increased budget and then what you need to do which is why is it really labor intensive is that you need to do it for every day and unfortunately it doesn't let you allow to choose days a week, it is just dates so you know if you want to test it for a couple of weeks you know you could test a month of turning on and off. So what this does is you've got your current daily budget which for us is £15. Now that is saying that is your base level so if you know that you don 't want to get as many leads on the weekend or you know that sales dip over a weekend what you want to do is to keep your budget consistent and then over Monday to Friday is increase your budget by a certain amount and that will then mean that over weekend you 're spending less and in the week you're spending more if that's how it's working for you.
[2:05] So on here you've got a couple of options you can change your start date so if we say on a Monday at like 7am UK time and then on a Friday at say 7pm we want to turn this daily budget increase amount off so what you can do you can do it by a percentage or you can do it by an amount so we're currently spending £15 a day and so I want to up it to £25 a day in the week so I know I can spend more so I would put in here the amount you want to increase by so it will then tell you here it will spend an average of £25 a day during that period which a £10 increase. Now what you then have to do if you want to do it for the following week is add another time period so this is where it gets get a bit time consuming and unfortunately it doesn't remember the time from you doing it from the week before so you need to then try that again up your spend and again same thing you can you can change your increase amount but it always either has to be a value or a percentage so once you've done that you can do up to 50 periods in a row so you might just want to do it all in one go or you might want to come in every week and just do it for the next week but see how it works for you and then once you've done that press publish and then all you'll notice in your performance results in the ad spend column that isn't the times that you've upped your ad spend so in Monday Friday in this case you'll see that increase and then when it comes down to Friday and over the weekend it will then level back out to your normal ad set budget or campaign budget a £15 a day so I hope that helps give it a test let me know what you think and hope that helps your results alright see you next time

*Video: lesson video hosted in Skool.*

In this quick video you will learn...

- How to build custom metrics for Hook & Hold Rates on your video ads
- How to add these to you Custom Columns
- What benchmark metrics you should be looking out for (from 2:25)

Got questions? Let us know in the post comment section below, Liv will come back to you asap.

### Video transcript (cleaned)

[0:00] Hello welcome back in this video. I just wanted to share a really great custom con you can create to know how your video is performing on engaging your audience. So it's called the hook rate and the hold rates. I wanted to walk you through how to set those custom columns up but also then how to look at those metrics and what they mean for your video creatives. Now the key thing is here the hook and hold rate only work for video based content so whether that's short form, long form, gifts it doesn't work for carousels or statics. So if you want to head into ads manager under the columns section here if you scroll down to custom columns and what you need to do is head to custom and within the create custom column metric click on there and the first thing we want to do is create our hook rate. So what we want to do here is a three second video play and we want to divide that by impressions. Now we want to call this our hook rate.
[1:03] I'm just going to call it hook rate two because I've obviously already got this but it's called a hook rate and your format wants to be percentage. Now then you can choose who you want to share this with either yourself or everyone else in the business. So you want to press create metric and then we want to create our second metric which is the hold rate. So same thing we want to go on to three plays and I want to divide that by impressions. Same thing here call it hold rate I'm putting hold rate two and then change the format to percentage. Now what these two metrics mean are the hook rate is the number of people that have seen your ad versus how many people have stayed for three seconds and then the hold rate is how many people have seen your ad but have watched the full thing.
[1:54] So now we've created those custom metrics we want to come back to custom columns and add in those metrics. So we want to get our hook rate and we want to get our hold rate and press save. Now this data will pull through and you'll begin to see it here. Now if you've got a static it will still pull some metrics through but you need to ignore them because there's not any three plays or three second views so they'll be slightly skewed. So we'll take this creative as an example. When we're looking at a hook rate we want a hook rate to be 25% or over as a really good marker. If it's lower than that doesn't mean it's very bad but obviously we use that as sort of like a benchmark and then our hold rate we want that to be around sort of like 10% ish. Now when you take that a little bit of a pinch of salt because if your video is under say 30 seconds you might see hold rates of more up to 15-20% but if your video is you know 60 seconds plus that might be slightly lower on that 5 to 10% mark because obviously with a world like TikTok or short form video content people you know aren't likely to stay for a whole video. Doesn't mean we shouldn't do that type of content it just means your percentages of the hold rate might be slightly lower which is equally okay. So that's how you create custom metrics for the hook and hold rate, what they mean and what to look out for. ## Meta Restricts Health Business Tracking

Source: https://www.skool.com/theadsclinic/classroom/8995064f?md=411456e9094c4fca9296396c13040edd

#### Lesson text

**(Here's How We Bypass It)**

If you're running Meta ads for health and wellness businesses, here's what's probably happening:

✅ Your campaigns deliver.

✅ People click.

🛑 But Meta shows zero conversion data.

You can't optimise. Columns stay blank. The algorithm is flying blind.

Here's what most advertisers don't realise -> 🚨This isn't a campaign problem. It's a Meta restriction problem.

When your business falls into the "health and wellness" category, Meta actively restricts how your conversion signals flow back into Ads Manager.

🛑 Weight loss? Blocked.  
🛑 Supplements? Blocked.  
🛑 Hormone clinics? Blocked.  
🛑 Functional medicine? Blocked.  
🛑 And many more....

The standard pixel simply can't send the signals Meta needs to optimise your campaigns.

So you're stuck running ads with one hand tied behind your back.

In this video, I show you:  
✅ Why Meta blocks conversion signals for health & wellness accounts  
✅ Why rewriting copy or changing creatives won't fix this  
✅ The tracking solution we're using to bypass these restrictions  
✅ Full walkthrough showing how to feed real conversion data back into Meta  
✅ This has already unlocked multiple client accounts that were stuck spending money with zero visibility.

[See the post below to watch](https://youtu.be/lW9GyPbbnrk)

If your health business ads feel impossible to scale, this is why.
